body.statement: \(G+\operatorname{Adm}(G)=G^\star\) and \(\mathcal I_E(G+\operatorname{Adm}(G))=\mathcal I_E(G)\), where \(\operatorname{Adm}(G)\) ranges over all absent directed edges and unordered bidirected edges, including both loop types, even when additions jointly change SCCs and create previously unoccupied bidirected rectangles.
body.justification: It turns global closure into edgewise saturation.
body.gap: Individual safety does not generally imply joint safety.
body.consumer: An oracle algorithm tests only one-edge additions.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove that the union of all individually admissible profile-changing edges is E-equivalent to the base graph.
obligation.obstruction: Individual signature preservation does not imply joint preservation for a general antitone independence map.  For this E-model the missing joint step is equivalent to the still-open unrestricted greatest-representative closure.
obligation.attempted: Singleton composition was used to turn each admissible one-edge extension into an E-equivalent graph, and the interval property was used in the reverse direction conditional on an in-class greatest representative.  This proves the exact identity conditionally but does not prove that the unrestricted union remains in the class.  The exhaustive sparse gate directly tested all-admissible unions in its finite region and found no failure.
obligation.partial_result:
Conditionally on unrestricted greatest-representative closure, the target reduces exactly to observable singleton signatures.  First, if \(e\in\operatorname{Adm}(G)\), then \(\Sigma_E(G+e)=\Sigma_E(G)\) by definition, and singleton composition gives \(G+e\equiv_EG\).  Hence \(e\in E(G^\star)\setminus E(G)\).  Conversely, if \(e\in E(G^\star)\setminus E(G)\), then
\[
 G\subseteq G+e\subseteq G^\star,
 \qquad G\equiv_EG^\star,
\]
and antitonicity gives \(G+e\equiv_EG\), hence \(e\in\operatorname{Adm}(G)\).  Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Adm}(G)=E(G^\star)\setminus E(G),
 \qquad G+\operatorname{Adm}(G)=G^\star,
 \qquad \mathcal I_E(G+\operatorname{Adm}(G))=\mathcal I_E(G).
\]
No positivity, rank, support, boundary, or limiting condition occurs: the argument is finite and purely graphical.  The unresolved premise is precisely that \(G^\star\equiv_EG\) for the unrestricted finite-DMG class.
